title: What If Earth Were Twice as Big?
description:
A new what-if every day at 5:48 pm (Riyadh).

If Earth were twice as wide and made of the same rock, it would have eight times the mass, and gravity at the surface would be twice as strong. You would weigh double from the moment you woke up: every step would feel like carrying a second you on your back. Leaving the planet would get much harder too. The speed needed to escape Earth's gravity would double, from about 11 km/s to about 22 km/s.

This assumes the same average density as today's Earth: surface gravity grows with radius times density, and escape speed grows with radius times the square root of density.
Sources: NASA Earth fact sheet (radius 6,371 km, surface gravity 9.8 m/s2, escape velocity 11.2 km/s).
Narration is AI-generated (ElevenLabs) and the pictures and clips are AI-generated. This is a thought experiment.

Could you live on a double-size Earth? Answer in the comments.
